name: feasibility_constrained_gaussian_rank_pairing
primary_law: Within each sex, generate Gaussian rank-priority scores with latent correlation 0.90. Traverse FVC in ascending order, adding all still-unassigned FEV1 rows satisfying FEV1 <= current FVC to a priority queue. Assign the eligible row with the smallest score. Without binding feasibility constraints this is Gaussian rank-copula pairing; with binding constraints it is the explicitly defined constrained allocation law.
score_construction: For m rows, draw m independent standard normals and sort them to obtain z. Independently draw m standard normals e. The score for ascending FEV1 row i is rho*z[i] + sqrt(1-rho^2)*e[i].
constraint: FEV1 <= assigned FVC, with equality allowed and no numerical tolerance.
tie_breaking: Equal priority scores are ordered by ascending within-sex FEV1 row index.
infeasible_marginals: Raise ValueError if any ascending FEV1 exceeds the corresponding ascending FVC. In that case no permutation can satisfy the constraint while preserving both columns.
population_weighting: Give each sex total weight 0.5, irrespective of block sizes. Within each sex give every row equal weight.
interpretation: An assumption-based synthetic pairing law, not an estimated source dependence or a validated model of the broader target population.
